text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- The government is likely to decide on whether to increase energy prices by December. If freed from the government control, the prices would probably increase by up to 35 percent.
- Brok is likely to become the third Polish brewery to enter the Warsaw stock exchange.
- The deputy president of Poland's crafts association said bread and roll prices should rise 60 percent by the end of the year.

- Some members of the Sejm's budget committee has proposed taxing secondary-market turnover in mass privatisation NFI units, though details from the finance ministry on who would pay and how much were not available.
- Gorazdze SA cement maker will take over a 60 percent stake in mineral mine Zielonogorskie Kopalnie Surowcow Mineralnych in several weeks.
- Poland may annul the tender for a supplier of anti-tank missles for a new combat helicopter.
- Assembly of Spain's Seats cars is to be launched in the western city of Poznan.

- South Korea's Daewoo is considering limiting its investment in Poland or withdrawing from agreements with the government because of trader Universal's launch of car assembly with Daewoo competitor Hyundai.
- Polisa SA insurer has asked the Securities Commission for a permission to enter the bourse's main market.
